approach: In crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, an item's second failure ends as `ItemEnd::Failed(Failure)` with `Failure { reason, shared: Option<String> }`. `shared` is Some only on positive evidence of a cause that is not a verdict on the item. Evidence is (a) `athena_core::disk::StopCause::of(reason).is_environment()` on a run that ended `Failed` or with no outcome, or on a read that ended in an Err with no job, or (b) a typed host error: a `GhFailure` (athena_core::gh, found by `downcast_ref`, which sees through anyhow context) with no HTTP status or a status of 401, 403, 429 or 5xx, found in the Err arm of `landing_from_report`. A run or read Err with no such evidence is per item. That covers every job-state bail (declined, running, interrupted, already closed, the readings cap, "verification does not hold"). `Drain::finish` passes a lone failure over with a note, like Paused and Skipped. It stops with `Stop::RepeatedFailure` only when an earlier different item holds the same shared key, with check and insert in one lock section. Keys: the StopCause kind for named environment causes, the masked text for OtherEnvironment, and `host: github <status>` for typed landing errors. Run and Read structs are unchanged. The classification is done by pure functions (`run_failure`, `host_cause`, `failure_key`) that are unit tested, and the drain tests drive them through `drain::drain` with scripted doubles.

decisions.choice: A no-outcome run or read Err is per item by default. It is shared only when `StopCause::of(text).is_environment()` holds for it. A `Failed` outcome is shared on the same test. Rejected, TimedOut and Failed with a Work reason are never shared. Run, Read and `RealSteps::run` get no new field and no new classification.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The Err sites are item-specific: run/mod.rs 340 declined, 348 running, 356 interrupted, 360 already closed; run/pin.rs 150 readings cap; run/close.rs 412 verification does not hold. `RealSteps::run` (drain.rs 3562) turns them all into `outcome: None`, so masked equal texts across items would stop the batch falsely. The typed host errors the Err arm already knows, `BudgetShort` and `LowDisk` (3564, 3575), set `held`, so they are never a Failed item. The only positive evidence left in a run or read Err is text that the shared classifier (disk.rs 388-415, also used by run/mod.rs and scope_guard.rs) reads as environment. The producer's usage-limit and expired-login stops arrive as `Failed` outcomes with those reasons, and the same test catches them.

decisions.choice: Add `Landing::HostError { why: String, key: String }`, returned only from the Err arm of `landing_from_report` (drain.rs 3056) when a new pure `host_cause(&anyhow::Error) -> Option<String>` finds a `GhFailure` with status None, 401, 403, 429 or 500..=599. It returns the key `host: github <status or no status>`. Any other Err (including GhFailure 404, 405, 422 and non-gh errors) stays `NotLanded(text)`, as does the Ok arm (3052). `Drain::land` handles HostError like NotLanded, writing `landing = "not landed: <why>"` and returning `LandStep::NotLanded { host_cause: Some(key) }`. NotLanded(why) and the after-rebase recheck give None. `RealSteps::land` (3607, `other => other`) passes the variant through. `landing_from_report` becomes `pub`.
decisions.reason: Same principle as decision 1, applied to the landing: where the error arises plus a typed fact decides, never text equality. A gh failure with no status or an auth, rate-limit or server status is about the host, shared by every item; a 404 or a refused merge is about one pull request. Red CI (Ok arm) is a verdict on the item. The key comes from the typed status, not from text, so the repository path with a pull-request number cannot defeat matching. Making the function `pub` lets criteria 3 and 4 use production landing values.

rejected.option: Treat every landing Err as shared (kept plan round 3)

decisions.choice: Keys. For LowDisk, CheckTimeout, ProducerAuth and UsageLimit the key is the StopCause Debug text. For OtherEnvironment it is `failure_key(reason, names)`. Helper `failure_key(text, names) -> Option<String>`: lower-case, split on whitespace, trim edge punctuation (backtick, parentheses, quotes, comma, colon, full stop, semicolon) and a trailing `'s`, mask whole tokens equal to a name (item or retry job), job-id-shaped tokens and all-digit tokens, join with single spaces. An empty result is None and never matches. `State.failures: Vec<(String, String)>` holds shared keys only.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3 and keeps whole-token masking, so item `a` cannot corrupt words. The wrapped-id forms are real: close.rs 348 writes run `athena go {id}` again, which gives the token `{id}` with a trailing backtick. Masking works only because edge punctuation is trimmed, so a unit test states it for backticks and parentheses.

decisions.choice: Check and insert into `State.failures` in one `self.st()` section in `Drain::finish`. After the lock is dropped, a match calls `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item.job))` with a note naming both items. No match notes `item X failed twice and is paused for this run: <reason>` and calls `pass_over`. The failed item stays in `report.queued` and is not tried again this run.
decisions.reason: Two concurrent workers (`drain_concurrent`) cannot both miss each other. It matches how Paused and Skipped behave and adds no Report field, so the JSON and the display prefix `repeated failure: item X failed twice` are unchanged. No Steps method is called with the lock held.

risks.risk: A true shared cause is missed, so the batch pauses items one at a time. Examples: a gh outage during a run, a Failed run with a non-environment text, or an OtherEnvironment text with per-item data that masking does not remove.
risks.mitigation: Named environment causes (429, 401, low disk, check timeout) are keyed by StopCause kind, not by text. Landing host errors are keyed by the typed status. Only OtherEnvironment text is masked. A miss pauses more items, each with a visible note, and the budget and job limit bound the run.

risks.risk: Two unrelated verdicts with the same fixed sentence (critic reject, planning cap, 'checks failed after rebase') are taken as a shared cause.
risks.mitigation: Only Failed or no-outcome results with an environment StopCause, and `Landing::HostError`, can be shared. Rejected, TimedOut, a Work-reason Failed, a pull-request-state NotLanded and the after-rebase recheck never are. Criteria 2 and 3 run the controls through the drain.

risks.risk: A gh failure with status None, 401 or 403 may be specific to one item (for example a pull request the token cannot read), so two such items would stop the batch.
risks.mitigation: A stop is the conservative outcome and a note names both items. 401 and 403 and an absent status are almost always about the token or network, shared by the whole repository. 404, 405 and 422 are per item. The criterion 4 unit test pins the split.

risks.risk: Tests could pass by relying on the stub's own text rather than on production classification.
risks.mitigation: The doubles return scripted `Run` and `Landing` values only. Shared causes use production constants and typed `GhFailure`, landings are built by the production `landing_from_report`, and the per-item controls use the real bail formats.

risks.risk: The Before::RepeatedFailure seeding runs two workers with timing waits, and a second failing item changes the order.
risks.mitigation: Reseed with `errors` for bad and bad2 and wait for the entry `end bad2-retry`. The loop already waits for the entry and then 150 ms for the stop to be stored. Keep the asserted row counts and run the whole file.

risks.risk: A failed item stays in `report.queued`, so the next `athena drain` retries it and a permanently failing item repeats across runs.
risks.mitigation: This matches Paused and Skipped items. The note says 'paused for this run'. A persistent pause would touch the scope guard, which is out of scope.

risks.risk: The new `Landing` variant and the `LandStep` and `RunStep::Failed` changes break matches elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: The compiler finds each one. The only matches on `Landing` and `LandStep` are in drain.rs, and the test doubles construct only `Landing::Landed` and `NotLanded`, which stay valid.

demonstrations.method: Serial `drain::drain(&stub, limits(9.0), &Quiet)` over a and b with the default Stub. a gets the default Rejected outcome both times; b lands. Assert on the stub log, `report.stop`, `failed_item`, `queued`, `landed` and the notes.

Each text uses the job's own name, so a and b texts are equal after masking. Extra control: both items end (Some(Failed), 'the producer did not complete: crashed') (a Work reason).
demonstrations.observes: In every case the log has `read c`, `run c` and `land c`. `report.stop` is not `Stop::RepeatedFailure`, `failed_item` is None and `landed == 1`. a and b are in `report.queued`. Notes say `item a failed twice and is paused` and `item b failed twice and is paused`, each with its reason.

demonstrations.method: Serial `drain::drain` over a, b, c with `Stub.runs` scripted as (Some(Failed), reason) for a, a-retry, b, b-retry. Cases: (1) reasons `format!("{}: success: API Error: 429 {{detail 1}}", athena_core::disk::USAGE_LIMIT)` and a different detail text for b; (2) `athena_core::disk::LOW_DISK` text, with a different tail for each item; (3) `athena_core::disk::PRODUCER_AUTH` text; (4) `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` plus other text with a job name inside, which exercises masking; (5) landing: a and b each run to Landed and `Stub.landings` hands back `landing_from_report(Err(GhFailure { call: "repos/o/r/pulls/7/merge" or "/8/merge", status_code: Some(503), text }.into()))`; (6) the same with `status_code: None`. demonstrations.method: Unit test `failure_key_masks_wrapped_ids` in drain.rs `tests::failure`, on the pure `failure_key`.
demonstrations.observes: `failure_key("run `athena go 20261103-162416-m9th` again", names)` equals `failure_key("run `athena go 20261103-170000-zzzz` again", names)`. The same holds for `(job 20261103-162416-m9th)` and `job 20261103-162416-m9th's verification does not hold`. A text of only names or digits is None. Item `a` does not change the word `checks`, and `failure_key("a failed", ["a"])` masks only the token `a`.

demonstrations.method: Review the diff of `Drain::finish`, and run the drain tests that drive both branches of it. Criterion 1's test drives the pass-over branch and criterion 3's test drives the stop branch.
demonstrations.observes: The `ItemEnd::Failed(failure)` arm no longer calls `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, ..)` unconditionally. It calls it only in the branch where an earlier different item has an equal shared key. Otherwise it notes `item X failed twice and is paused for this run: <reason>` and calls `pass_over(&item.job, ..)`. The check and insert share one `self.st()` section. A `grep` for `Stop::RepeatedFailure` in drain.rs shows no other setter.

demonstrations.method: Review the text of drain.rs, display.rs and CHANGELOG.md, and run a display test that renders `display::drain(&report)` for a and b, where a is rejected twice and b lands.
demonstrations.observes: The rendered text names a and a-retry with outcome `rejected` and reason `ended rejected`, and has the note `item a failed twice and is paused`. For the shared-cause stop the text still starts `repeated failure: item b failed twice` and adds `for a cause shared with an earlier item (see notes)`. `git diff -- CHANGELOG.md` shows an Unreleased/Changed entry naming the root cause (`finish` stopped the batch for one item's double failure) and the new rule. The drain.rs module header (about 103), the docs of `Stop::RepeatedFailure` (about 942) and `meaning()` (about 1001), `Report::failed_item` (about 1051), `State.stop` (about 1120) and the `Landing` variants state the new rule. `cargo test -p athena-cli --lib` still passes the `Stop::ALL` meaning test.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the pass-over dropped a's job lines or its note, the rendered text would not name a or its rejection and the assertions would fail.
